title: Topology variants + planner/executor
acceptance_criterion: Selection follows measured utility; a simpler workflow may win
verdict: The variants exist, terminate, and share a budget; the decision to ship 'fixed' is recorded. But the comparison that is supposed to justify it is degenerate — tools are stubbed everywhere, so 'selection follows measured utility' is not actually demonstrated. NOT complete.
evidence: src/agentops_workbench/graph/{single_agent,planner_executor,topology}.py; TOPOLOGIES registry has 3 entries; tests/graph/test_topology.py = 11 tests pass (termination, max-steps, shared budget constants)
docs/adr/0006-topology.md records 'fixed graph is the default'
experiments/held-out-v1: fixed vs single_agent compared; single_agent burned 2-10x completion tokens for 0/12 vs 0/12 task_success
gaps: Tool dispatch is stubbed in BOTH variants: single_agent.py:60 '# Tool dispatch is a stub for MVP; step 6 wires real MCP calls' and planner_executor.py:72 same. Step 6 never did this.
tool_correctness = 0.0 on all 24 held-out runs — no topology ever issues a correct tool call, so the 'matched-budget comparison' compares three tool-less answer generators.
planner_executor was not included in the held-out run (selected_topologies = [fixed, single_agent]); it ships untested against the benchmark.
The ADR-0006 'simpler workflow wins' conclusion rests on token count, not on measured task utility (which is 0 for every variant).

synthesized.note: The /dev-kit:build runner was never executed in this monorepo.
